Gloria Bangura knows the events she personally experienced or was told through dialogue up through scenario 4: she had observed Donald seeming distracted, asked if he was okay, suggested professional help, worried she may have overstepped, apologized, heard Donald say it was okay and that he knew she meant well, and then felt relieved because she believed the apology had been well received and the tension had eased. She also knows she wants to strengthen their professional relationship and invites Donald to collaborate on an upcoming project; she knows Donald accepts and says he wants to be more involved.

Gloria does not know Donald’s private internal state beyond what he said or what she inferred. She does not objectively know whether he truly forgave her, whether his job dissatisfaction came from deeper personal issues, or whether professional help would actually benefit him. At the point of scenario 4, she also does not yet know the future scenario 5 events, such as Donald’s renewed enthusiasm or his later appreciation for public acknowledgment.

In scenario 4, Gloria’s belief that her apology was effective and her resulting relief do not directly cause her to give professional help or make amends. Instead, that positive belief and relief motivate her intention to strengthen her professional relationship with Donald, which leads her to invite him to collaborate on the new project.

ANSWER: e
